judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the "COMPRE AGORA" button on the second hero slide (/verao). It uses the inverted glass variant: the live CSS gives it background-color var(--dark-glass-800) = #00000072 (about 45% black) with white text, over the light slide image. In Rampa's own crop of that slide the button background samples at #7c7e7f to #797a7a, which gives 4.08:1 to 4.31:1 against #ffffff for 16px regular text. I found no default state that passes (only the hover state darkens it), no large-text exemption, and nothing wrong with the measurement. It fails 1.4.3.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is footer payment icon #1 of 7. The SVG source and the crop show the Pix logo. All seven brand logos (Pix, Apple Pay, Mastercard, Visa, Elo, Diners, Amex) have the same alt="payment", it is still there in the live HTML, and no visible text near them names the accepted methods. The logos carry information (which brand is accepted) that "payment" does not give, so the alt is not an equivalent. The image does not literally show something unrelated: the alt is a generic placeholder. Read fairly, though, the claim that the alt does not describe what the image shows names the real 1.1.1 failure, and the fix it points to (name the brand) is the right one. If someone treated the logos as decorative, a non-null placeholder alt would still fail under F39.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is a 20px benefit-bar icon (a dollar sign in a circle) next to the h4 "15% OFF NA PRIMEIRA COMPRA", which states the whole benefit in text. Its alt "Ícone representativo do benefício" ("icon representing the benefit") is literally accurate: the image is an icon standing for that benefit. So the claim that the alt describes something the image does not show is wrong. The icon is redundant with the adjacent text and carries no information the alt fails to convey. The only arguable 1.1.1 problem is a different one: a decorative image with a non-null, meaningless alt (F39), whose fix is alt="", not a better description. The finding does not name that problem.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the footer newsletter field (input type="email", aria-label "Insira seu e-mail para receber novidades", placeholder "Insira seu e-mail"). It asks for the user's own email address, one of the input purposes listed for 1.3.5. Neither the input nor its form has an autocomplete attribute. type="email" only sets the data format; it does not identify the field as the user's own email, and the sufficient technique (H98) is autocomplete="email". I found nothing that makes it pass. It fails 1.3.5.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the "Feminino" desktop main-menu link text: 14px, regular, color var(--color-neutral-50) = #fff. It sits in the floating header pill, whose CSS background is var(--dark-glass-800) = #00000072 (about 45% black) over whatever lies behind it: the hero carousel, or page content when the sticky header floats as the page scrolls. The reported #8d8d8d is exactly that glass over white (3.32:1). Over the second hero slide (light #dfe2e6 behind this text in Rampa's own crop) the glass gives about #7c7e7f, 4.1:1. Over the first slide this spot is partly over dark hair, but the text still falls below 4.5:1 in normal, reachable states. Caveat: the header is missing from Rampa's full-page screenshot and crops, so I rebuilt the measured state from the CSS and the hero pixels; it is consistent with the report. It fails 1.4.3.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the "Novidades" desktop main-menu link text: 14px, regular, white (#fff), on the header's dark-glass-800 background (#00000072) over the hero or the page content behind the sticky header. On the default first slide this spot is over dark hair and would pass. Over the second hero slide (light #e0e3e5 behind this text in Rampa's crop) the glass gives about #7c7e7f, 4.1:1, which matches the reported 4.00 to 4.25:1. It would be lower still over white page content. The text therefore misses 4.5:1 in normal, reachable states of the rotating carousel and sticky header. Caveat: the header is missing from Rampa's screenshots, so I rebuilt the measured state from the CSS and the hero pixels. It fails 1.4.3.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the second hero slide image, inside the link to /verao. Its alt is the CMS creative code "HOME_GERAL_TV1_ALTO_VERAO"; the live page data shows the field "creative" being used as alt. The image is an image of text ("NOVA COLEÇÃO", "Confira os lançamentos da estação") with a model, and that text appears nowhere else. The link's accessible name becomes "HOME_GERAL_TV1_ALTO_VERAO COMPRE AGORA". An internal identifier is not a text alternative (F30), and the alt does not convey what the image shows, as the finding says. It fails 1.1.1.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the first hero slide image, inside the link to /tudo-com-60. Its alt is the CMS creative code "HOME_GERAL_TV1_TUDO_COM_60". The image is an image of text: "NOVAS PEÇAS | NOVOS DESCONTOS", "SALDOS", "TUDO COM 60%OFF" and a disclaimer. The countdown bar repeats only "TUDO COM 60% OFF + FRETE GRÁTIS", so most of this text is available nowhere else. A code-like identifier is not an equivalent (F30), and the alt does not describe what the image shows. Even if the banner were judged redundant, the non-null placeholder alt would still fail (F39). It fails 1.1.1.
